beats.title: Cardigan's First Eisteddfod
beats.description: A Welsh prince invited poets and musicians to compete at his newly built castle, the first recorded gathering of its kind.

beats.title: Messiah Premieres in Dublin
beats.description: A charity concert in an Irish music hall gave the public its first hearing of a sacred oratorio now sung every winter.

beats.title: Royal Fireworks Music Rehearsal
beats.description: Some twelve thousand people paid to hear a rehearsal of Handel's outdoor suite in a London pleasure garden, jamming the roads.

beats.title: Haydn's London Concerts
beats.description: An ageing Austrian composer crossed the Channel to conduct a season of public concerts that made him a star in Britain.
beats.note: Salomon concerts began in 1791 and ran to 1795.

beats.title: Beethoven's Fifth and Sixth Debut
beats.description: A freezing, four-hour benefit concert in Vienna introduced two symphonies, a piano concerto and a choral fantasy to the public.

beats.title: Beethoven's Ninth Premieres
beats.description: A deaf composer stood on stage as an orchestra and chorus performed his choral symphony, and the crowd cheered wildly.

beats.title: Mendelssohn Revives Bach's Passion
beats.description: A young conductor in Berlin staged a concert of a long-forgotten Baroque passion, sparking a revival of its composer.

beats.title: Paganini's London Debut
beats.description: A fabled Italian violinist, rumoured to have sold his soul, thrilled and scandalised Londoners with double-priced tickets.

beats.title: Liszt Sparks Lisztomania in Berlin
beats.description: A pianist's recital tour sent audiences into a frenzy of fainting and souvenir-hunting, a century before screaming pop fans.
beats.note: Berlin recitals began late December 1841; some sources date the fever 1842-44.

beats.title: Jenny Lind Tours America
beats.description: A Swedish soprano promoted by P. T. Barnum drew frenzied crowds on a concert tour across the United States.

beats.title: Boston's World Peace Jubilee
beats.description: A mammoth festival in a purpose-built coliseum featured thousands of singers, a giant orchestra and a visiting Waltz King.

beats.title: Carnegie Hall Opens
beats.description: A new New York concert hall began its life with a gala week in which a famous Russian composer conducted his own music.

beats.title: The First Promenade Concert
beats.description: A London concert series began with cheap standing tickets, bringing orchestral music to a wider audience every summer since.

beats.title: Mahler's Symphony of a Thousand
beats.description: A composer conducted over a thousand performers in a vast hall, and the audience gave a half-hour ovation.

beats.title: Hollywood Bowl's First Season
beats.description: A natural hillside amphitheatre in Los Angeles opened its first official run of outdoor concerts under the stars.

beats.title: Rhapsody in Blue Premieres
beats.description: A young composer sat at the piano in a New York concert billed as an experiment in modern music and introduced a jazz-tinged hit.

beats.title: Benny Goodman at Carnegie Hall
beats.description: A swing clarinettist brought his jazz band to a classical temple, and the audience stomped for more.

beats.title: Marian Anderson at Lincoln Memorial
beats.description: Barred from a Washington hall, a contralto gave an open-air Easter concert before a huge crowd beneath a statue of a president.

beats.title: Ellington's Carnegie Hall Debut
beats.description: A bandleader unveiled a long jazz suite on the history of his people at a benefit concert in a New York hall.

beats.title: The Moondog Coronation Ball
beats.description: An Ohio arena oversold a rhythm and blues dance and is often called the first rock and roll concert, ending in chaos.

beats.title: First Newport Jazz Festival
beats.description: A Rhode Island seaside town hosted the first annual jazz festival, becoming a template for outdoor music gatherings.

beats.title: First Newport Folk Festival
beats.description: A Rhode Island seaside festival put young folk singers on stage, launching a gathering that later hosted a famous controversy.

beats.title: Dylan Goes Electric at Newport
beats.description: A folk hero plugged in a guitar before a stunned festival crowd, drawing boos and cheers in equal measure.

beats.title: Woodstock
beats.description: Hundreds of thousands of fans packed a New York dairy farm for days of music, mud and peace.

beats.title: The First Glastonbury Festival
beats.description: A few thousand people paid a small fee and got free milk at a Somerset farm, starting Britain's best-known festival.

beats.title: The Band's Last Waltz
beats.description: A Thanksgiving farewell concert in San Francisco united a Canadian-American group with a parade of guest legends.

beats.title: Simon & Garfunkel in Central Park
beats.description: A reunited duo played a free show to an estimated half-million people on a New York lawn.

beats.title: Live Aid
beats.description: Simultaneous concerts in London and Philadelphia raised money for famine relief before a huge global television audience.

beats.title: Three Tenors in Rome
beats.description: Three famous opera singers joined forces in ancient Roman baths for a concert that became the bestselling classical record.

beats.title: Freddie Mercury Tribute Concert
beats.description: Rock stars filled Wembley Stadium to honour a late frontman and raise money for AIDS charities.

beats.title: Coachella Is First Held
beats.description: A two-day festival in a California desert polo field began as a rival to mainstream festivals and became a giant.

beats.title: Concert for New York City
beats.description: Rock, pop and soul stars filled Madison Square Garden to honour first responders after a devastating attack on the city.

beats.title: Live 8
beats.description: Concerts in several world cities ahead of a leaders' summit urged action against poverty, twenty years after a similar event.

beats.title: Tupac Hologram at Coachella
beats.description: A computer-generated image of a rapper killed years earlier performed on stage alongside two live stars at a desert festival.

beats.title: Beychella at Coachella
beats.description: A pop superstar headlined a desert festival with a marching-band-and-step-team show that became a landmark concert film.

beats.title: One World: Together at Home
beats.description: Stars performed from their living rooms in a lockdown livestream honouring health workers.

beats.title: Taylor Swift's Eras Tour Begins
beats.description: A record-setting stadium tour spanning every era of a pop star's catalogue opened in Arizona.
